interpretation: A test reference is evidence to inspect, not satisfaction of every clause. The merging reviewer must examine the complete original normative document, not only this matrix.

criteria.title: No additional discovery surface
criteria.original_statement: When the artifact capability is installed, existing public command, agent, top-level skill and persistent tool registrations shall gain no new entries.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Locally exercised: the captured pre-engine command, agent, top-level-skill and persistent-tool sets are unchanged; startup fixtures are byte-bound and negative controls reject /ca:spec, a persistent artifact tool and eager schema loading. Hosted exact-head proof remains pending.

criteria.title: Explicit spec contracts and honest drafts
criteria.original_statement: When validating a specification for readiness, the engine shall require observable contract records and explicit intent relationships while allowing incomplete structural drafts.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: The 0.3.x content model differs from reviewed schema 0.2.0. Readiness checks presence/relationships, not prose truth; review every original content obligation.

criteria.title: Plan binding and bidirectional coverage
criteria.original_statement: When validating an implementation plan, the engine shall resolve its spec binding and every task-to-criterion reference and reject an invalid dependency graph.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Local pair binding and coverage/DAG checks run. Existing plan-producing/consuming host workflows are not end-to-end qualified.

criteria.title: Stable symbol identity
criteria.original_statement: When records are edited, reordered or retired, the engine shall preserve existing symbol identities and never reuse a retired identifier.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Local stable IDs, retirement and duplicate authority checks run. Review rename/import behavior in the actual repository history.

criteria.title: Canonical HTML with detectable view drift
criteria.original_statement: When rendering a valid model, the engine shall emit one deterministic HTML artifact whose visible normative content matches the embedded model.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Normal engine reads reject model/view drift. Byte-preserving prior-candidate reads are tested; manual integration must not bypass the parser.

criteria.title: Offline branded human review
criteria.original_statement: When a valid spec or plan is rendered, the complete document shall remain readable offline with codeArbiter branding or a validated repository-owned replacement.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Offline Chromium and local branding tests are available. No cross-browser/native accessibility qualification or automatic repository branding-configuration discovery is claimed.

criteria.title: Bounded contextual reads
criteria.original_statement: When an agent requests a symbol, the engine shall return complete records and explicit context completeness at a single model revision.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Whole-record contextual reads and forward progress are checked. Real-host context budget and complete dependency/use-site closure remain to review.

criteria.title: Typed operations and inert input
criteria.original_statement: When processing an internal request, the engine shall accept only the closed versioned operation grammar and shall never execute specification or plan content.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Closed inert operation protocol is exercised. Invocation through each host permission boundary is not fully wired.

criteria.title: Conflict-safe writes
criteria.original_statement: When two cooperating writers use the same previous model identity, at most one shall replace the artifact and the other shall receive a conflict without changing it.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Linux and Windows cooperative writer/CAS/replay/recovery tests run. macOS exact-host and physical power-loss/network-filesystem guarantees remain unqualified.

criteria.title: Repository and executable trust
criteria.original_statement: When resolving artifacts, assets or the executable, the integration shall reject escapes and untrusted binary substitution.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Anchored Linux and root-handle Windows paths plus installation-pinned bridges pass locally. macOS and every real host permission boundary remain to qualify.

criteria.title: Approval is a governed transition
criteria.original_statement: When recording approval, the workflow shall bind its existing authority source to the exact normative content and reject ordinary edits that attempt that transition.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Cooperative receipt checks are implemented; actual user/SMARTS/reviewer event capture is not fully integrated. Synthetic tests are not production approval.

criteria.title: Changed contracts block stale execution
criteria.original_statement: When a spec or normative plan changes, consumers shall reject stale bindings before dispatch, resume, farm projection or acceptance.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Local normative binding/freshness rejects stale content. Outer workflow resume and reapproval flows require target-host tests.

criteria.title: Evidence-backed task acceptance
criteria.original_statement: When a task is marked ACCEPTED, its current identities, verification and required reviews shall all be present and valid under the existing workflow.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Named-test checks and declared-task input coverage are strengthened. Actual runner adapters and complete dependency/environment input closure remain required.

criteria.title: Interruption-safe, deadlock-free scope execution
criteria.original_statement: Within an execution scope, the coordinator shall permit verified provisional dependencies without claiming acceptance, and shall accept the scope only after final-snapshot verification and combined-diff quality review.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Engine scope transitions and stale-evidence revalidation run locally. A fresh native-candidate fixture proves interruption at REVIEW and atomic scope acceptance, but full real-host caller checkpoint/resume behavior is not integrated.

criteria.title: Existing workflow end-to-end integration
criteria.original_statement: When a full-lane feature or sprint runs, existing producer and execution routines shall consume the HTML pair through the shared protocol with unchanged governance checkpoints.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Canonical feature/sprint pilot routing exists and fresh native-candidate fixtures cover typed authoring, dispatch, stale blocking, resume and atomic acceptance. These are synthetic workflow-authority fixtures, not complete real-host feature/sprint traces; do not report the criterion fully satisfied.

criteria.title: Explicit intent coverage without false proof
criteria.original_statement: When checking new-format intent coverage, the engine shall resolve scope-to-criterion relationships and report unsupported/missing input instead of treating it as an empty successful check.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Structured scope links replace Markdown heuristics for typed specs. External issue-checkbox checking remains a heuristic and cannot prove intent completeness.

criteria.title: HTML discovery and correct cache invalidation
criteria.original_statement: When a governing spec changes or is imported, context discovery shall reflect current validated HTML metadata without hiding invalid new-format records.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Candidate advisory hook wrapper and mocked seam tests only; run actual cache/dedup/receipt freshness suites on all generated hosts.

criteria.title: Derived farm compatibility
criteria.original_statement: When exporting a farm slice, the adapter shall derive the existing closed runtime JSON from a current approved HTML plan and preserve its narrow-test and review requirements.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Locally implemented: minimal current-slice projection, source/spec/plan/slice/ID/base/RED binding, pre-canary source validation, provider-only enrichment, exact execution-byte/provider seals, and shared built-dispatcher enforcement all have fresh native-candidate fixtures. This is not promotion evidence: real authority adapters, installed host payloads, exact-head generated-host/CI proof and a fresh frontier/low-tier model matrix remain required; June 2026 earns zero current credit and HTML farm use stays disabled.

criteria.title: Loss-aware legacy import
criteria.original_statement: When converting a legacy feature spec/plan, import shall preserve source provenance and report ambiguous or missing meaning without manufacturing approval or evidence.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Explicit line-mapped pair import is exercised. An exact-candidate native-Windows pilot preserved draft/unverified authority and transferred no approval; human-reviewed mappings and old-approval disposition remain required for production files.

criteria.title: Recoverable pair cutover and rollback
criteria.original_statement: When switching a reviewed spec/plan pair to HTML, the system shall expose one live authority per artifact and stop execution during an interrupted or conflicting cutover.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Journaled pair cutover/guarded rollback runs on Linux, with native Windows storage primitives separately qualified. The exact-candidate Windows pilot restored both legacy files byte-for-byte and removed both HTML authorities; the full Windows semantic suite, macOS exact-host and production-host recovery remain open.

criteria.title: Consumer closure across canonical and generated sources
criteria.original_statement: Before default enablement, every identified spec/implementation-plan producer and consumer shall be updated, explicitly compatible, or explicitly excluded with a tested reason.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Partial: the inventory-led closure gate accounts for entry/resume, planning/TDD/execution, context, status/doctor/startup/commit, farm, migration, CI, published instructions, generated copies and explicit exclusions. Entries marked pending still require their named runtime integration and host evidence before default enablement.

criteria.title: Trusted native binary distribution
criteria.original_statement: When the capability is installed, the host shall select a matching reviewed binary without requiring an end-user Go toolchain or runtime downloads.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Linux and Windows native builders and pinned bridges pass. The release-only boundary rejects linked/replaced roots, fake architectures and unsupported identities, requires qualification receipts bound to exact commit, protected workflow run, platform, digest and named native tests, and is fed by a separately required three-host aggregation job. Linux and Windows cold execution pass from every staged package root without Go, PATH or network fallback while the ordinary installer remains fail-closed. Actual release-channel application, hosted macOS and published provenance remain incomplete.

criteria.title: Platform-tested write and recovery guarantees
criteria.original_statement: Before marking a native platform supported for new artifact writes, its actual replacement, locking and recovery behavior shall pass fault and concurrency tests.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Linux and Windows named process-death, locking and replacement tests pass; macOS compiles and vets but awaits exact-host CI. No physical power-loss or remote-filesystem certification.

criteria.title: Safe HTML and adversarial parsing
criteria.original_statement: When artifact content or branding contains hostile text, the parser and renderer shall reject or inertly escape it without executing code or corrupting symbol boundaries.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Fresh Windows conformance rejects duplicate JSON, appended executable script content, renderer drift and remote-reference SVG logos, and re-runs the strict parser/resource/inert-content suites against one exact candidate. Required Linux/macOS exact-head execution and remaining real-host seams are still open.

criteria.title: Separated identities and reproducible hashes
criteria.original_statement: When normative content, execution state or presentation changes, the engine shall update only the corresponding identities under the declared canonicalization profile.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: A Python stdlib serializer independent of the Go canonicalizer verifies pinned current-schema normative/model/render identities, and a real task-start transition proves revision/model advancement without normative drift. The safe-integer/string canonical profile matches the original contract; hosted exact-head cross-platform qualification remains open.

criteria.title: Capability diagnostics and conservative legacy behavior
criteria.original_statement: When the new capability is absent, unsupported or not enabled, existing legacy workflows shall remain explicit and new-format workflows shall not fall back to ungoverned free-form writes.
criteria.implementation_notes_and_gaps: Explicit engine/bridge failures and legacy isolation have local tests and published guidance. The evidence-backed rollout decision keeps legacy behavior as the default; actual all-host cold-install/production-resume handling remains to exercise.

final_review: Consolidated regression suites; whole-feature acceptance remains pending.
